item.title: Try it on 耍花招，试探底线
item.description:
节目简介

“Try it on” 的字面意思是 “穿上试试”。在口语中，这个短语不仅可以表示 “试穿” 衣服，还能用来描述 “试图通过耍小聪明、钻空子来达到目的的行为”，甚至还可以表示 “故意提出过分要求，试探他人的底线”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 学习这个短语的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
Are you coming to that meeting later?

Phil
Um, no, I'm leaving early. I'm… erm… going to the airport. I'm going on holiday and I need to get there early.

Feifei
Wait a minute, you're not going on holiday. I don't believe you. You're just trying it on! That important football match is on this afternoon. You just want to go and watch that.

Phil
Maybe… OK, if you promise not to tell anyone else, I'll explain what 'try it on' means here.

Feifei
OK, deal. Everyone knows 'try it on' can be used to talk about clothes. But this is different, isn't it?

Phil
Yes, this is about lying. One meaning of 'try it on' is to try to deceive someone so you don't get in trouble. If someone lies to get out of work early, then they're 'trying it on'.

Feifei
Yes, it's an expression that we often use to challenge someone. This means we often used it in the negative. 'I know you're not going to the airport, don't try it on.'

Phil
Let's hear some more people using 'try it on' in this way.

Examples
My sister said she's got no money and asked to borrow my credit card to buy some food from the shops, but I saw a massive parcel with her name on it. She's just trying it on.

So, the waiter in the restaurant I went to last night didn't bring me back any change after I paid. They said that they'd just forgotten, but I think they were trying it on.

My landlord raised my rent by £100 without telling me. They're definitely trying it on.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习短语 “try it on” 的用法。动词 “try” 的意思是 “尝试”。“Try it on” 原本的含义很简单，指的就是 “在挑选衣服的时候穿上试试”。不过，在口语中，“try it on” 也可以表示某人 “试图通过欺骗、装无辜或耍小聪明来达到目的”。比如，如果你觉得一个人在故意编造借口、夸大事实或试图蒙骗你的时候，你就可以说对方是在 “trying it on”。

Phil
Yes. And it also has another meaning. 'Try it on' can also mean to behave badly to test someone's limits.

Feifei
“Try it on” 不仅可以表示 “试图通过欺骗他人来达到目的”，还可以形容 “故意惹事、无理取闹、挑战规则，借此激怒别人或试探对方的底线”。

Phil, you've got teenage children, haven't you?

Phil
Yes, teenagers are notorious for sometimes trying it on to see what their parents will let them do, like using their phones after we've told them to stop. It means I need to say "Don't try it on! I've told you to put your phone away".

Feifei
OK. That's it for this programme but join us again next time. We really can help you improve your English. We're not just trying it on!

Phil
See you next time!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: Non-starter 注定行不通的计划，无法接受的条件
item.description:
节目简介

常有人说：“Well begun is half done（好的开始是成功的一半）”。而在英语中，如果有一个想法太过离谱，听起来 “注定行不通，甚至不值得一试”，就可以用 “non-starter” 来形容。在谈判中，人们还会用 “non-starter” 指那些 “触碰底线、完全无法接受或没有讨论余地的条件”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 学习复合名词 “non-starter” 的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
What are you working on there, Phil?

Phil
I've been putting together a business idea: mail-order coffee.

Feifei
What's that?

Phil
Yeah, you could have an app, and then when you fancy a coffee, you press a button, and someone makes you one and sends it to you through the post.

Feifei
Um… I think that's the worst business idea I've ever heard. In fact, I'd say that's a complete non-starter.

Phil
Hm… Maybe you're right. I'll have to think of something else. In the meantime, let's look at that expression 'non-starter'. Can you explain it, Feifei?

Feifei
Yes, we describe something as a non-starter if we think it has absolutely no chance of succeeding. I think a mail-order coffee business is pretty much guaranteed to fail – it's a non-starter.

Phil
It's an expression that we can use to talk about a business idea, but it's also something that can be about any plan, project or initiative. We often use the expression to say that something hasn't been approved.

Feifei
Yes. So, it's also what we use to reject a proposal. For example, 'I've seen your suggestion, but I'm sorry, that's a non-starter'.

Let's listen to some other people using the expression 'non-starter'.

Examples
I've got some friends who live in Scotland. They've invited me up to their house for Christmas, which is great. But they want me to go for a freezing cold swim in the sea on Christmas day, and that is a non-starter.

You want me to leave at 6.30 in the morning for this hike? That's a non-starter.

I pitched an idea at work to make a podcast series about monkeys learning English. My boss said it was a non-starter.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “non-starter” 的用法。“Non-starter” 是一个复合名词，字面意思是 “无法开始的事情”。在实际使用中，它常被用来比喻那些 “一开始就注定难以成功、听起来就没有希望实现的计划、提议或想法”。

除此之外，在谈判和讨价还价的时候，我们也可以用 “non-starter” 来描述 “完全无法接受、连考虑余地都没有的条件或提议”。换句话说，如果某个条件触碰了底线，以至于谈判根本无法继续进行，那么这个条件就是一个 “non-starter”。

Phil
Yes, it might come from horse-racing, where a horse that just stays at the start line and refuses to run is described as a 'non-starter'. Literally, it didn't start the race.

Feifei
OK. That's it for this programme but join us again next time. When it comes to ideas, learning English is definitely not a non-starter, and we have lots of different ways to help you!

Phil
See you next time!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: No notes 无可挑剔，十分完美
item.description:
节目简介

如果学生在作业或考试中表现不佳，老师通常会留下 “notes（批注，评语）”。而当一个人的表现 “无可挑剔，近乎完美” 时，我们就可以用 “no notes” 来形容。“No notes” 还有哪些地道的用法？听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起学习吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you? Have you had a good week so far?

Georgie
I really have, actually. I went to a concert, it was one of my favourite bands, and the singer was incredible. My sister even put me on her shoulders for my favourite song. I loved it – no notes. How about you?

Feifei
That sounds brilliant, Georgie! I'm having a great week too. The weather's been lovely, I've managed to get all my work done on time, and I've even had time to meet friends after work! No notes.

Georgie
That sounds wonderful, Feifei. I'm so happy for you! Now, let's learn the expression 'no notes'.

Feifei
Yes. Use 'no notes' when you want to say something is perfect. 'Notes' in this context refers to feedback or criticism, just like when a teacher assesses a piece of work and leaves notes for future improvement.

Georgie
Right. So, if you say 'no notes', you are expressing that you have no feedback or criticism. Whatever you're talking about is perfect or flawless.

Feifei
So, you used it in the context of a singer's performance. I used it when talking about my perfect week. Now, time for some more examples.

Examples
That three-course meal was incredibly delicious. No notes.

I went to a wedding, and the best man's speech was hilarious. No notes.

Wow. Your outfit is stunning. No notes.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “no notes” 的用法。单词 “note”指的是 “批注” 或 “评语”。所以，“no notes” 听起来像是在说 “批改作业或试卷时没有留下任何修改意见”，而我们实际上用它来表示 “我觉得这件事无可挑剔、十分完美，一点意见也没有。”

Georgie, is the expression 'no notes' always used on its own, without a verb?

Georgie
Yes. Most commonly, it is used on its own, but you might also hear a sentence like 'I have no notes'.

Feifei
在使用 “no notes” 的时侯，我们既可以单独使用它，强调某事 “很完美，没什么可挑剔的”，也可以把它放在句中使用，比如，“I have no notes”，意思就是 “我没意见，我完全同意”。

Georgie
OK, let's recap. 'No notes' is a modern slang expression that is used when something is perfect, and no negative feedback is needed.

Feifei
Thank you for joining us. Goodbye!

Georgie
Bye-bye!

item.title: Say less 懂了，不必多说
item.description:
节目简介

就像 “say no more” 的意思并非字面上的 “别说了”，而是在告诉别人 “你不用再说了，我都懂” 一样，新兴表达 “say less” 的意思也不是 “少说点”，而是 “我懂了，你不用再多说了，我完全同意”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起来学习这个年轻一代常用的新潮表达。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
I'm very well, thank you Feifei. How are you?

Feifei
I'm very well too, thank you. Now, it's time to introduce a new expression to our listeners. I think let's teach a modern phrase this time, Georgie. Have you got any of those?

Georgie
Say less, Feifei.

Feifei
What? Are you telling me to stop speaking?

Georgie
No! I mean I understand. I'm with you! Let's teach a modern expression.

Feifei
Is 'say less' a modern expression?

Georgie
It is. 'Say less' was popularised on social media and is used in informal, everyday speech. You can use 'say less' when you understand someone fully and don't need further explanation, or when they've suggested a great plan and you don't need further convincing.

Feifei
OK, but it sounds quite friendly, so I guess it's used to show enthusiastic agreement, rather than hinting that someone should stop speaking.

Georgie
Exactly. Shall we hear some more examples?

Feifei
Say less, Georgie.

Examples
My boss asked me if I was ready to go on a break after a 15-hour shift. I said, "Say less! Get me out of here."

My friend said the dress code for their party was 'all black', and I said, "Say less! I don't have anything colourful in my wardrobe."

You're asking me if I want an ice cream on this boiling hot day? Say less!

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习流行表达 “say less” 的用法。“Say less” 的字面意思是 “少说点”。但它的实际含义和表达 “say no more” 非常接近，就是 “我明白你的意思了，不用再多说了” 或者 “我完全同意”。相比之下，“say less” 不仅更加简短，也更具现代感和潮流感。

Georgie
That's right. And there are some other, similar expressions too. If a good plan has been suggested, of course you could say 'say less', but you could also say 'I'm in' or 'I'm sold' if you've been persuaded. Shall we grab coffee after this, Feifei?

Feifei
I'm sold on that idea, Georgie.

在口语中，如果别人提出了一个我们赞同或支持的意见、想法或计划，除了用 “say less” 表示赞同之外，我们还可以用 “I'm in” 和 “I'm sold” 来回应。“I'm in” 的意思是 “算我一个” 或者 “我加入”；“I'm sold” 的意思是 “你把我说服了，这个想法我买账”。

Georgie
OK. Time to recap. Use 'say less' when you want to enthusiastically agree with someone after they have suggested something.

Feifei
Thank you for joining us. Goodbye!

Georgie
Bye-bye!

item.title: Share your life story 把人生故事全讲出来了
item.description:
节目简介

正如字面意思所言，“life story” 指的就是一个人的 “人生故事，人生经历”。虽然每个人的人生故事都独一无二，但并不意味着每次交流都需要事无巨细地讲给别人听。因此，表达 “share your life story” 除了表示 “分享你的人生故事” 之外，也常用于比喻或讽刺一个人 “讲得过于详细、过于冗长，把不必要的背景和细节一股脑儿都说出来”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 一起学习 “share your life story” 的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei and I'm joined by Becca. How are you, Becca?

Becca
I'm well, thanks! I had such a great weekend! I caught up with my friend. Well, she lives outside of London with her husband now, but we've been friends since we were 11, and we basically grew up together in London. And we went to a market that we used to go to often, because we studied textiles together and used to go to this market all the time for fabric. Anyway, she now works in marketing and is doing really well for herself and…

Feifei
Whoa, whoa, whoa, Becca. I asked how you are, but I didn't ask for you to share your life story.

Becca
Haha. OK, Feifei. I'm doing fine thanks. You used an interesting expression there – share your life story.

Feifei
Yes, a life story is a narrative about a person's life experiences. It's often very long and it goes into incredible detail of the events, relationships, and milestones that helped shape that person's identity.

Becca
Yes, so if we share our life story, it could feel like we're over-sharing, that we're saying far too much than necessary. And you said you didn't ask for my life story, because I was rambling on and going into detail about my friend.

Feifei
Yes, you were going into very specific details. And though it's sometimes nice to share about yourself, you should remember, when a British person asks you, 'how are you?' or 'are you alright?' it's usually a very basic greeting that requires a simple response. Let's hear some more examples.

Examples
I remember my grandpa always sharing his life story with me. Usually the same stories, but I didn't mind.

I love when I meet new people when I'm travelling and they share their life story with me. It's so interesting to learn about different cultures and upbringings.

Sorry I'm late! I was talking to the receptionist, and he was sharing his life story.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “share your life story” 的用法。“Life story” 指的就是一个人的 “人生故事，生活经历”。因此，“share your life story” 字面的意思就是 “分享你的人生故事”。不过，在口语对话中，这个表达常常带有调侃或者讽刺意味，用来形容一个人 “讲得过于详细、过于冗长，把不必要的背景和细节全都交代出来，仿佛要把自己的人生故事从头到尾讲上一遍”。它通常用于形容一种 “oversharing（过度分享）” 的情况。

Becca
We often use the expression 'share your life story' in a slightly negative way, usually in response to someone talking at length. So, it's important to be mindful of how you say this expression. If you raise your tone towards the end, it could express surprise and feels more positive. But if you drop your tone, it could express disappointment or even sarcasm.

Hear the difference – 'I didn't ask for you to share your life story,' and, 'I didn't ask for you to share your life story'.

Feifei
You're right, the latter sounded a bit rude.

在使用中，我们可以通过不同的语气来表达对他人分享的故事感到惊讶、感叹甚至是讽刺。比如，语气上扬的 “You are welcome to share your life story!” 往往是在邀请别人 “你也来分享一下你的故事吧！”，而语气下降的 “I didn't ask you to share your life story” 则是在抱怨 “我又没让你讲人生故事，你也说得太长了”。

Becca
That's it for this programme! Join us next time for more useful English expressions. Goodbye!

Feifei
Goodbye!

item.title: Keep yourself to yourself 不爱与人交往，喜欢独来独往
item.description:
节目简介

人人都有自己的天性。有人喜欢积极地和他人交流，也有人喜欢通过独处来 “恢复能量”。在英语中，我们可以用 “keep yourself to yourself” 来形容那些 “不爱与人交往，喜欢独处，甚至给人一种神秘感” 的人。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too. I'm Feifei.

Becca
And I'm Becca.

Feifei
Becca, our new office neighbour seems nice, but I hardly ever see him talking to anyone.

Becca
Yes, he really seems to keep himself to himself.

Feifei
Hmm, what does that mean?

Becca
If someone keeps themself to themselves, they don't spend much time socialising with other people. They prefer to be on their own and usually don't share much about their personal life. Someone who is introverted could prefer to keep themself to themselves.

Feifei
So, does it mean they're unfriendly?

Becca
Not at all. Someone who keeps themself to themselves can be perfectly friendly. It just means they're private or quiet. It usually has a neutral description, although sometimes people use it to suggest someone who is a bit mysterious.

Feifei
Ah, I see. Now, let's hear some more examples.

Examples
I'm just going to keep myself to myself today. I'm so tired.

I've been trying to get to know my new neighbour recently, but I think she likes to keep herself to herself.

When I go travelling on my own, I usually want to meet up with people, but there are others who just want to keep themselves to themselves.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “keep yourself to yourself” 的用法。“Keep yourself to yourself” 的字面意思是 “把自己留给自己”，但实际上它用来形容一个人 “不太与他人来往，不喜欢交谈和社交”。这个说法通常并不带有责备的意味，不是说某人是个 “闷葫芦”，而只是比较直接客观地描述一个人 “性格比较内向，更喜欢独处，甚至可能显得有些神秘”。

Becca, can I say 'keep ourselves to ourselves'?

Becca
Yes, you absolutely can! You can change the pronoun depending on who we're talking about. She could keep herself to herself, or if there's a lot going on, I might want to keep myself to myself.

And with a very different meaning, if we say 'we keep something to ourselves', it means we're keeping a secret or just aren't sharing it. I guess it has a similar mysterious feeling to 'keep yourself to yourself'.

Feifei
我们还可以用和 “keep yourself to yourself” 类似的表达 “keep something to oneself” 来形容某人 “把事情放在心里，保守一个秘密”，或者 “独自占有某样东西，不与他人分享”。Well, Becca, I'm glad you didn't keep this expression to yourself and instead decided to share it with us.

That's it for this programme. Join us next time for more useful English expressions. Goodbye!

Becca
Bye!

item.title: One size fits all 均码，一刀切
item.description:
节目简介

在购买帽子、手套等小件服饰时，我们经常会看到 “one size fits all（均码）” 的商品，意思是 “一个尺码适合所有人”。如今，“one size fits all” 已被引申用来形容那些 “不顾个体差异、对所有人或所有情况都采用同一种解决方案” 的做法，类似于汉语中的 “一刀切”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 一起学习 “one size fits all” 的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil. Hi Feifei, I've got the new team t-shirts – have this one. They're one size fits all.

Feifei
But this is enormous? One size fits all? I'm not sure it does.

Phil
OK. But it does help us tell people about the expression 'one size fits all'.

Feifei
It's sounds like something you would use to talk about clothes.

Phil
Yes, and that's where it comes from. Clothes are sometimes sold as 'one size fits all'. It's sold as one size, and it's supposed to fit everyone.

Feifei
Well, I'm not sure it works for these t-shirts, but I can imagine it working for something like a hat. We don't just use it to talk about clothes, do we?

Phil
No, we don't. It's become more general. 'One size fits all' is often used to describe a way of doing something where everyone is treated in the same way. A training programme for a company might be described as one size fits all – everyone does the same training. A one-size-fits-all approach to problem-solving means trying to solve every problem the same way.

Feifei
Yes, and in the same way that one-size-fits-all clothes don't always fit everyone, this expression is sometimes used negatively. For example, we might describe something as 'one size fits all' to suggest that it ignores the needs of individuals or a particular situation

Phil
Let's hear some more people using the expression 'one size fits all'.

Examples
Me and my cousin are such different people. I mean I always try to find creative ways to deal with problems, but he always takes a one-size-fits-all kind of approach.

I need to order some new computer software for the office. Everybody uses things slightly differently, they've all got different requests, but I'm hoping we can get something that's one size fits all that we can all use.

When I go to the barbers, it doesn't matter what I ask for, they give me the same haircut. It's one size fits all in there.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们在学习表达 “one size fits all” 的用法。“One size fits all” 的字面意思是 “同一个尺码谁都可以穿”，原本被用来形容服装的尺码，也就是 “均码”。久而久之，人们也用这个表达来形容那些 “用同一种方式对待所有人或事物的一刀切做法”，通常带有批评或反对的意味。

不过要注意，这个表达有两种用法。没有连字符的 “one size fits all” 是一个短语，可以用来形容一件衣服的尺码，或者描述一个人 “试图用同一套解决方法来应对不同的问题”。而加上连字符的 “one-size-fits-all” 则是一个复合形容词，通常用在名词前。比如，“a one-size-fits-all solution” 指的就是 “一套一刀切的、通用的解决方案”。

Phil
Yes, other expressions that are similar are 'off the peg' or 'off the shelf'. They can be about clothes – meaning standard sizes that haven't been fitted or tailored. But we can now use them to talk about products or ways to solve problems. 'An off-the-shelf solution' or 'off-the-peg solution' is a standard way of doing things – it hasn't been adapted to a specific situation.

Feifei
同样源自服装或零售业的类似表达还有 “off the peg” 和 “off the shelf”，它们的意思都是 “标准的，现成的”。在日常生活中，这两个表达都可以用来形容那些 “一成不变的，甚至有些死板的产品、方法或手段”。

Phil
OK. That's it for this programme, but join us again next time. We have lots of different ways to help you learn English because when it comes to learning a language, one size doesn't fit all.

Feifei
See you next time!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: Side quest 让人分心的支线小插曲
item.description:
节目简介

明明是要出去买菜，却被突然冒出的想法或路上看到的新鲜事所吸引，结果做了许多计划之外的事情……在英语中，这种生活或工作中 “让人分心的小插曲” 被称为 “side quest”。“Side quest” 虽然会让人暂时偏离原本的计划，却往往充满趣味，甚至带来意想不到的收获。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 一起学习这个流行表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei, and here comes…

Phil
… I'm Phil. How are you doing, Feifei?

Feifei
Where were you?

Phil
Sorry, I just went shopping to buy something for dinner. I say I went to buy something for dinner, but then I ended up on a side quest and bought a load of records.

Feifei
And got back here late, I see. I would be annoyed, but actually that expression 'side quest' would be a good one to learn.

Phil
OK. Yeah, good idea. To explain this one, we have to talk about video games. In many games, you have a main quest. That's the main thing that you have to do in the game. A side quest is not the main thing you have to do. It's something else you can do that's often short and fun.

Feifei
Right, that's in a video game. But in your shopping trip today, your main quest was to buy something for dinner. But then you got distracted by something more fun and went to buy records. That was your side quest.

Phil
Yes, that's right. We can use 'side quest' to talk about things that you do that aren't the most important thing. And yes, they're often something that you enjoy doing.

Feifei
Well, I'm glad you had fun! Let's hear some other people using 'side quest'.

Examples
We've always wanted to visit Belfast for the scenery, but there were just these beautiful museums that we found on a side quest wandering around the city.

I was on my way to a concert, and I had loads of free time, so I went on a bit of a side quest to a bookshop.

I had loads of things to prepare for a presentation at work, but then I realised the painters were out of ink, so I went on a bit of a side quest to try and get that fixed first.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们在学习流行语 “side quest” 的用法。“Side” 的意思是 “一旁的，侧面的，次要的”。“Side quest” 原本指的是 “某个电子游戏或故事的剧情中与 ‘main quest（主要任务，主要情节）’ 无关的支线剧情或小插曲”。而现在，不少人也会略带调侃地用 “side quest” 来形容那些 “跟原本要做的事情无关，让人分心、甚至忘记正事的日常琐事” 或 “小插曲”。

Phil
Yes, we have quite a few expressions where we use the word 'side' to talk about something less important. A side dish is something that you eat that goes with the main dish. A side hustle is a job that you do that's not as important as your main job, and it might give you a side income.

Feifei
在英语中，单词 “side” 还可以用来形容其它 “次要的、辅助性的” 事物。比如，“side dish” 指的就是 “和主菜相搭配的配菜”；“side hustle” 通常指 “主业之外的兼职” 或 “副业”；而 “side income” 指的就是一个人的 “额外收入” 或 “副业收入”。

Phil
OK. That's it for this programme, but join us next time to make sure that your English learning is more than just a side quest.

Feifei
See you then!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: Passing ships 如擦肩而过的航船，难得相遇
item.description:
节目简介

有人把人生比作汪洋大海，而每个人都是一条在风浪中行进的小船。虽然大海无边无际，但船只的航线也总有交汇的时刻。英语表达 “passing ships” 就用 “交错驶过的船只” 来比喻两个人 “即使相隔不远，但因为生活忙碌而难得见上一面” 的场景。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
I'm very well, thank you, Feifei. How are you?

Feifei
I'm very well, thank you, Georgie. I haven't seen you much lately. What's going on?

Georgie
I know! I think our schedules are quite different at the moment. Whenever I'm at my desk, you seem to be in meetings, and then when you're back at your desk, I'm doing something else, somewhere else in the office building. We're like passing ships at the moment! 

Feifei
Passing ships. That's the expression we're learning in this programme. The longer version is 'like ships that pass in the night'. 

Georgie
Yeah, so let's actually imagine that. Two ships at night. They briefly see each other in the darkness, and then they continue in different directions. The encounter is brief and the people on board the ships probably don't have time to speak to each other. 

Feifei
Right. So recently, our schedules are different, so we're not seeing each other very much, and when we do, the interaction is very short. We're like passing ships. 

Georgie
Yeah. Hopefully our schedules line up a bit soon, so we can catch up! 'Passing ships' is often used to talk about busy adult life when two people are finding it hard to meet.  

Feifei
That's right. Let's hear some more examples from our BBC Learning English colleagues.  

Examples
I really need to meet up properly with my neighbour like have dinner. We talk a lot over the fence, but we never have time. It's like we're passing ships. 

My brothers and sister always seem to visit my town when I'm away, so I never get to catch up with them. We're like passing ships. 

I've got a colleague I get on with really well, but we work different shifts, so we're like passing ships! We only see each other for a couple of minutes every time.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “passing ships” 的用法。“Passing ships” 是一个名词短语，字面意思是 “互相驶过彼此的船只”，它形容人们 “行色匆匆，擦肩而过” 的场景。

这个表达传递出的感觉，和它更完整的说法 “like ships that pass in the night” 很相似：两个人像是在黑夜中偶然相遇的小船，打了个照面后，便各自回到原本的航线，消失在夜色之中。所以，我们经常用这个表达来感叹 “生活太忙碌，即使在同一个地方，我们也总是完美错过，想见一面真的不容易”。

Georgie
Now, because we're comparing ourselves to passing ships, we often use the word 'like' – we're like passing ships. We can also make the metaphor stronger by removing 'like' – we're passing ships at the moment.

Now, another phrase that expresses a similar idea is 'cross paths'. Again, you can imagine this literally – two people walking on separate paths which then meet. But metaphorically it means that two people's lives intersect in some way.  

Feifei 
是的，除了 “passing ships”，我们还可以用 “cross paths” 来表达类似的含义。短语 “cross paths” 的意思是 “路线发生了交汇”，人们通常用它来比喻 “偶然相遇，和彼此发生了交集”。

Georgie
OK, so for example, my best friend and I crossed paths at university, but we didn't become friends until much later. 

Feifei
Great. Now let's recap. We learnt the expression 'passing ships', which means that two people are on different schedules and are limited to brief encounters.

Georgie
Thanks for joining us. Goodbye!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: Understood the assignment 交出满分答卷，干得漂亮
item.description:
节目简介

老师问你 “Do you understand the assignment?”，意思是 “你明白布置给你的作业是什么吗？” 不过，如果有人对你说 “You really understood the assignment!”，意思就变成了夸你 “干得真漂亮！”为什么同一句话，时态一变，意思就完全不同？听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起学习流行语 “understood the assignment” 的意思和用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you? What have you been up to this week?

Georgie
Well, something that's really exciting is that I went to a costume party. Um. The theme was 'fairytales', and my friend came as a fairy. She wore these amazing purple wings, she got her makeup and hair done professionally, and she looked incredible. She really understood the assignment.

Feifei
Oh wow, that sounds fun! But what do you mean she 'understood the assignment'? Assignments are usually something we do at school, like essays and coursework, but you're talking about a costume party.

Georgie
Yes. That's because 'understood the assignment' is now being used as a slang phrase, meaning that someone did something very well – they exceeded expectations. So, at the party I went to, lots of people didn't really make much of an effort, but my friend went out and bought accessories, she did her makeup…

Feifei
Right, so she knew what she had to do to impress people, and she achieved that. She understood the assignment.

Georgie
Yes, exactly.

Feifei
Oh, interesting. Well, I'd like to hear some more examples to fully understand the phrase.

Examples
I told my wife I wanted to eat something unusual and special for my birthday, and we had the most amazing meal in the craziest restaurant I've ever been to. She really understood the assignment.

We're hoping to get our bathroom redone this year, and we just got the designs through, and the designer really understood the assignment. It looks so amazing and so relaxing. I can't wait to get it done.

I asked the band to write a catchy, three-minute pop song with an unforgettable chorus, and they totally understood the assignment. I can't get it out of my head!

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习流行语 “understood the assignment” 的用法。“Understand the assignment” 的字面意思是 “理解一项任务的目标，知道该怎么完成”。不过，它的过去式 “understood the assignment” 已经演变成了一个流行语，用来夸奖某个人 “非常清楚自己的角色和任务，分寸拿捏到位，把事情完成得极其漂亮，甚至大获成功”。

OK, Georgie, I think I've got another example. I asked you to teach us an expression that you might not find in a typical dictionary, and you really understood the assignment.

Georgie
That's a great example, Feifei! And thank you very much. One thing to note is that we usually hear it in the past tense. That's because it's used to comment on what someone has done after it has happened as a way to compliment or praise them.

Feifei
是的。虽然 “understand the assignment” 夸奖一个人 “知道自己要做什么” 也不算错，但人们还是更常在他人成功之后，用这个表达的过去式 “understood the assignment” 来给出评价和赞美。除此之外，我们还可以用类似的表达 “go above and beyond” 来夸奖一个人 “为了追求极致，付出了额外的努力，表现超出预期”。

Georgie
Yes. 'Go above and beyond' means that a person does more than is required for the task.

Feifei
OK, let's recap. We learnt the expression 'understood the assignment', which we can use to praise someone when they knew exactly what they had to do, and did it well.

Georgie
Thanks for joining us. Bye!

Feifei
Bye!

item.title: On to something 有了重大发现，想法很有道理
item.description:
节目简介

表达 “on to something” 听起来简短，但它其实可以用来表达 “有了一个很有道理的新想法”，或是 “发现了一条非常有价值的线索”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 一起学习这个表达的用法，以及它和 “into something” 之间的区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Becca
And I'm Becca.

Feifei
You look very excited. What's going on?

Becca
Well, I think I've finally figured out how to improve my video edits. I might be on to something!

Feifei
Ooh, that's interesting. But what do you mean by 'on to something'?

Becca
If you're on to something, it means you think you've discovered an important idea, or clue about it. Maybe you noticed something that other people haven't noticed yet.

Feifei
I see. So, for example, if detectives find a new clue, they might say, 'We're on to something.' And it's usually a positive expression?

Becca
Yes. It suggests progress or a good idea. Maybe not a complete answer yet, but you're moving in the right direction.

Feifei
OK. Let's hear some more examples of this expression 'on to something'.

Examples
Ah, so you think it's the foxes that are eating the rubbish? I think you're on to something.

I hadn't thought of doing it like that. But you know what? I think you're on to something.

She's tried putting rhubarb in the tart. Everyone else thinks it's a weird idea, but I think she's on to something.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “on to something” 的用法。如果我们对一个人说 “I think you are on to something”，意思就是 “我认为你的想法很有道理”；同时，它也可以用来形容 “你顺藤摸瓜，有了一个非常重要的新发现”。

Becca, what else do we need to know about 'on to something'?

Becca
Don't confuse 'on to something' with 'into something' because they mean very different things. If you're 'into something', it usually means you enjoy it or are interested in it.

Feifei
是的，大家注意别把 “on to something” 和 “into something” 搞混了。如果你 “into something”，通常是指你 “非常喜欢或对某事物很感兴趣”。

Becca
I think we're on to something with this programme.

Feifei
We are. And join us next time to learn more English phrases and expressions. Goodbye!

Becca
Bye!
